syllabus.verbatim: The Syllabus for General Intelligence would include questions of both verbal and non-verbal types. The test may include questions on analogies, similarities, differences, space visualization, problem-solving, analysis, judgment, decision-making, visual memory, discrimination, observation, relationship concepts, arithmetical reasoning, verbal and figure classification, arithmetical number series, etc. The test will also include questions designed to test the candidate's ability to deal with abstract ideas and symbols and their relationships, arithmetical computations, and other analytical functions.

Questions will be aimed at testing the candidate's general awareness of the environment around him and its application to society. Questions will also be designed to test knowledge of current events and such matters of everyday observations and experience in their scientific aspect, as may be expected of any educated person. The test will also include questions relating to India and its neighboring countries, especially pertaining to History, Culture, Geography, Economic Scene, General Polity and Scientific Research, etc. These questions will be such that they do not require a special study of any discipline.

Engineering Mechanics, Solid Mechanics, Structural Analysis, Construction Materials and Management, Estimating, Costing and Valuation, Concrete Structures, Steel Structures, Surveying, Soil Mechanics (Geotechnical Engineering), Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics, Hydrology and Irrigation Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Transportation (Traffic) Engineering.

syllabus.heading: Engineering Mechanics
syllabus.verbatim: System of forces, free-body diagrams, equilibrium equations; Internal forces in structures; Friction and its applications; Centre of mass, Moment of Inertia.

syllabus.heading: Solid Mechanics
syllabus.verbatim: Bending moment and shear force in statically determinate beams; Simple stress and strain relationships; Simple bending theory, flexural and shear stresses, Uniform torsion, buckling of column, combined and direct bending stresses.

syllabus.heading: Structural Analysis
syllabus.verbatim: Introduction to Statically determinate and indeterminate structures; Method of superposition; Analysis of trusses, arches, beams, cables and frames; Slope deflection and moment distribution method; Influence lines.

syllabus.heading: Construction Materials and Management
syllabus.verbatim: Construction materials: Bricks, Stones, Timber, Steel, Cement, Aggregates, Plastics, Polymers, Glass, Concrete, concrete mix design, testing of concrete. Construction Management: Types of construction projects; Project planning and network analysis - PERT and CPM.

syllabus.heading: Estimating, Costing and Valuation
syllabus.verbatim: Fundamentals of estimating, Cost Estimates for works, Rate Analysis, Valuation, Detailed Estimates.

syllabus.heading: Concrete Structures
syllabus.verbatim: Working stress and Limit State design concepts; Design of beams, slabs, columns; Foundation and Retaining Walls; Bond and development length.

syllabus.heading: Steel Structures
syllabus.verbatim: Working stress and Limit state design concepts; Bolted connections, Welds, Design of tension members, compression members and beams; Concept of plastic analysis - beams and frames.

syllabus.heading: Surveying
syllabus.verbatim: Principles of surveying; Errors and their adjustment; Maps - scale, coordinate system; Distance and angle measurement: Chain and Compass survey, Plane table surveying, Levelling and trigonometric levelling; Traversing and triangulation survey; Total station; Tacheometric surveying, Theodolite Surveying, Advanced surveying equipment.

syllabus.heading: Soil Mechanics
syllabus.verbatim: Three-phase system and phase relationships, index properties; Unified and Indian standard soil classification system; Permeability - one dimensional flow, Seepage through soils – two-dimensional flow, flow nets, uplift pressure, piping, capillarity, seepage force; Principle of effective stress and quicksand condition; Compaction of soils; One-dimensional consolidation, time rate of consolidation; Shear Strength, Mohr's circle, effective and total shear strength parameters, Stress-Strain characteristics of clays and sand.

syllabus.heading: Fluid Mechanics
syllabus.verbatim: Properties of fluids, fluid statics; Continuity, momentum and energy equations and their applications; Laminar and turbulent flow; Flow in pipes, pipe networks; Concept of lift and drag.

syllabus.heading: Hydraulics
syllabus.verbatim: Forces on immersed bodies; Flow measurement in channels and pipes; Channel Hydraulics - Energy-depth relationships, specific energy, critical flow, hydraulic jump, uniform flow.

syllabus.heading: Hydrology
syllabus.verbatim: Hydrologic cycle, precipitation, evaporation, evapo-transpiration, watershed, infiltration, unit hydrographs, hydrograph analysis, reservoir capacity, flood estimation and routing, groundwater hydrology - steady-state well hydraulics and aquifers; Application of Darcy's Law.

syllabus.heading: Irrigation
syllabus.verbatim: Types of irrigation systems and methods; Crop water requirements - Duty, delta, evapo-transpiration; Gravity Dams and Spillways; Lined and unlined canals, cross drainage structures.

syllabus.heading: Water and Wastewater Quality and Treatment
syllabus.verbatim: Basics of water quality standards – Physical, chemical and biological parameters; Water quality index; Unit processes and operations; Water requirement; Water distribution system; Drinking water treatment. Sewerage system design, quantity of domestic wastewater, primary and secondary treatment. Effluent discharge standards; Sludge disposal; Reuse of treated sewage for different applications.

syllabus.heading: Air Pollution
syllabus.verbatim: Types of Pollutants, their sources and impacts, Air Pollution control, Air Quality Standards, Air Quality Index and limits.

syllabus.heading: Municipal Solid Wastes
syllabus.verbatim: Characteristics, generation, collection and transportation of solid wastes, engineered systems for solid waste management (reuse/recycle, energy recovery, treatment and disposal).

syllabus.heading: Transportation Infrastructure
syllabus.verbatim: Geometric design of highways - cross-sectional elements, sight distances, horizontal and vertical alignments. Geometric design of railway Track – Speed and Cant.

syllabus.heading: Highway Pavements
syllabus.verbatim: Highway materials - desirable properties and tests; Desirable properties of bituminous paving mixes; Design factors for flexible and rigid pavements; Design of flexible and rigid pavement using IRC codes.

syllabus.heading: Traffic Engineering
syllabus.verbatim: Traffic studies on flow and speed, peak hour factor, accident study, fundamental relationships; Traffic signs; Signal design by Webster's method; Types of intersections; Highway capacity.

differences:
The repo's src/lib/ssc-je-civil-syllabus.ts is built from the 2025 notice (Notice_of_adv_je_2025.pdf) and is now superseded for the 2026 cycle. Comparing that 2025 notice against the 2026 notice I opened (both downloaded and extracted in this task):

1. Scheme numbers unchanged: Paper-I is still 50/50 + 50/50 + 100/100 with 0.25 negative marking, qualifying only; Paper-II Civil & Structural is still 100 questions/300 marks with 1.0 negative marking, 2 hours (2h40m for scribe-eligible). One procedural change: the answer-key challenge fee dropped from ₹100/question (2025, para 13.8) to ₹50/question (2026, para 13.14).

2. Paper-I syllabus restructured: 2025 listed Part-A (Civil Engineering) as two blocks — "Building Materials, Estimating, Costing and Valuation, Surveying, Soil Mechanics, Hydraulics, Irrigation Engineering, Transportation Engineering, Environmental Engineering" plus a separate "Structural Engineering: Theory of Structures, Concrete Technology, RCC Design, Steel Design" (this is exactly the flat 14-topic list the repo currently stores as SSC_JE_CIVIL_SYLLABUS_TOPICS). The 2026 notice replaces this with one flat, differently-named 13-item list: "Engineering Mechanics, Solid Mechanics, Structural Analysis, Construction Materials and Management, Estimating, Costing and Valuation, Concrete Structures, Steel Structures, Surveying, Soil Mechanics (Geotechnical Engineering), Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics, Hydrology and Irrigation Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Transportation (Traffic) Engineering." Several 2025 topic names (Building Materials, Theory of Structures, Concrete Technology, RCC Design, Steel Design) do not appear as such in 2026; they have been absorbed into or renamed as Construction Materials and Management, Structural Analysis, Concrete Structures, and Steel Structures.

3. Paper-II Part-A syllabus was rewritten from a narrative, paragraph-style description per topic (Building Materials; Estimating, Costing and Valuation; Surveying; Soil Mechanics; Hydraulics; Irrigation Engineering; Transportation Engineering; Environmental Engineering; plus a separate 'Structural Engineering' block covering Theory of Structures, Concrete Technology, RCC Design, Steel Design) into a more granular, differently-organized 21-heading structure (see the syllabus rows above) with materially different content emphasis — e.g. explicit new sub-areas such as 'Construction Management: Types of construction projects; Project planning and network analysis – PERT and CPM', an explicit 'Air Pollution' heading with Air Quality Index language, 'Municipal Solid Wastes' as its own heading, and 'Traffic Engineering' naming 'Signal design by Webster's method' and 'Design of flexible and rigid pavement using IRC codes' — none of which are named the same way, if at all, in the 2025 text.

4. Scope of the exam itself grew: the 2026 notice adds new streams not present in 2025 — Part-D (Computer Science & IT), Part-E (Electronics & Telecom), Part-F (Physics) for IMD Scientific Assistant posts, and Part-G (Telecommunications) for JE (Telecom) — reflected in its title 'Junior Engineer Examination, 2026 (Including IMD Scientific Assistant & DoT Telecom)'. This doesn't affect Civil content but does affect the exam-wide scheme table structure (more OR-branches in Paper-I/Paper-II subject rows).

Net effect for the app: src/lib/ssc-je-civil-syllabus.ts's SSC_JE_CIVIL_SYLLABUS_TOPICS list is stale for the 2026 cycle and should be replaced with the 2026 Paper-I Part-A topic list and/or the more detailed Paper-II Part-A heading structure above (the app should decide which granularity it wants to seed). src/lib/ssc-je/config.ts already correctly cites the 2026 notice number (HQ-C-3019/1/2026-C-3) in its header comment, so that file's citation is current; I did not audit whether its actual syllabus/scheme data (not shown to me — only the header comment) matches the verbatim text captured here.
caveats:
1. Notice board listing page (ssc.gov.in) is JavaScript-rendered, so WebFetch could not list entries directly; PDF discovery relied on (a) the URL pattern used by the existing 2025 reference in the repo, and (b) third-party news sites (career.aglasem.com, testbook.com, etc.) reporting the exact filename Notice_of_adv_je_2026.pdf and notice number. I only treat as "verified" what I actually opened via a direct https://ssc.gov.in/... PDF fetch with a captured HTTP 200 and byte size; the addendum row is explicitly flagged as unverified for this reason.

2. I could not find or open the 10.09.2026 addendum PDF itself despite trying multiple plausible ssc.gov.in filenames (all returned HTTP 404). Its existence and scope (IMD Scientific Assistant EQ only, not touching Civil syllabus/scheme) rests on secondary-source reporting, not a primary document I opened. If precision here matters for the app (e.g. an audit trail), this should be resolved by locating the exact PDF before the app claims "verified against addendum."

3. PDF text extraction (pdfplumber) initially mangled a couple of characters via kerning artifacts (e.g. a decorative "1." bullet before "General Intelligence & Reasoning", and "G eneral" with a spurious space) — I re-extracted the affected page with `pdftotext -layout` to confirm the clean, correct wording before reporting it verbatim; all syllabus text in this response has been checked this way, not taken from a single raw extraction pass.

4. I did not attempt to read src/lib/ssc-je/config.ts's actual syllabus/scheme data structures (only its header comment, which already cites the correct 2026 notice number) — comparing that file's stored data against the verbatim text above is a follow-up the app team should do; I focused on getting the official verbatim text, per the task's objective.

5. "Marks" and "questions" in the scheme table are reported as I read them from the notice's own table cell "Number of Questions / Maximum Marks" (e.g. "50/50" meaning 50 questions, max 50 marks — 1 mark per question, consistent throughout Paper-I; Paper-II Civil is 100 questions/300 marks, i.e. 3 marks per question). I split the combined cell into separate questions/marks fields for the schema; the citation still points to the single source table cell.

6. I did not check for a Hindi-language version of the notice, or whether SSC published a separate short-syllabus/exam-pattern circular outside this notice (none found in searches); the 97-page notice's paras 13 and 14 appear to be SSC's complete and only statement of scheme and syllabus for this cycle.

7. Scratchpad PDFs (je2026.pdf, je2025.pdf, notice_16092026.pdf, full_text.txt, full_text_16sep.txt, je2025_syllabus_pages.txt) were downloaded/written only to /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/ssc — never into the repo — per the task's instruction.
